note:
Coverage. All 28 physical pages were read at text level and all 33 measured regions were inspected on a crop: p4, p5, p7, p8 (whole block), p9, p15 (both objects), p16, p17 (both), p19 (three objects), p21 (both), p22, p23, p24 (whole block) and p25. Every printed exhibit in the paper is one of those regions, which is what makes this the lane's second exact census: fourteen exhibits, fourteen measured regions as anchors, no declared gap and no forced row. The reason is mechanical and it is the inverse of every booktabs paper in the block - the two weight tables here are not ruled grids at all, they are drawings pasted in as vector blocks, and the clustering pass follows ink, so it sees a picture of a table while it misses a table made of three rules. 

The census arithmetic. Thirty-three regions on eighteen of twenty-eight pages: eleven figure anchors, three table anchors and nineteen exclusions. The exclusions are thirteen pasted display equations (p7 the membership function, p10 twice, p12 twice, p13 twice, p17 the K-means distance, p19 three times - including the unnumbered brace-delimited optimisation model, the only equation in the paper the prose never numbers), two red resale banners (p18, p25 top) and four fragments: Table 1 arrives as three vector blocks on p8 and Table 3 as three on p24, so two blocks of each are fragments of a recorded exhibit. The convention is the same as every split figure in this lane: the anchor bbox is the largest fragment, because the validator only accepts a measured region, and the recorded area is the union of the fragments, because the union is what the page shows. That difference is the whole point on this paper - the Table 1 anchor reports 0.096 of the page and its union is 0.245, and the union of Table 3 is the largest exhibit in the document at 0.247 against Figure 1's 0.181. 

The caption system, which is this paper's signature fault. Fourteen exhibits, fourteen captions, not one of them says a thing: all bare noun phrases of six to seventeen words, none naming a variable, none naming a unit, none stating a condition, none drawing a conclusion. A reader who reads only captions learns that there is a framework, a tipping point and an optimal allocation, and learns nothing about what any of them measured. The one piece of information the captions do carry is the panel key on a wrapped second line, and that is where they fail twice: Figure 10 prints '(a)Afghanistan' welded to its letter, and every one of the seven two-panel figures prints the letters a second time inside the artwork at the top-left of each panel, where the left letter is clipped by the text margin and survives as a bare ')'. The form is 'Figure <n>:' with a colon for figures AND tables, unlike the no-colon house style of several papers in this block. 

Numbering and citation. Number order and page order agree except twice: Figure 7 is named on p19 and prints on p21, Figure 10 is named on p22 and prints on p23. Both are backward pointers and both are the same habit - the paper places a figure where it finishes drawing it and reads it on the page before. Against that, citation is the densest in the lane: all fourteen exhibits are named by number at least once, the framework pyramid carries six pointers, the sensitivity pair four, and the radar pair three. There is no under-cited exhibit and no positional-only pointer anywhere in 28 pages. 

Charts. Eleven figures and not one colourbar; eight of the eleven are two-panel composites drawn from the same authoring pipeline, one raster holding both panels with duplicated legends, and five of those pairs are the same three series (Precipitation, Arable land, Temperature) or the same model family (Smaller / Normal / Bigger state) re-run on a different computation. THE HABIT THAT COSTS THE PAPER ITS ARGUMENT: no two panels of any figure share a window - Figure 5 runs 0.25-0.31 beside 0.36-0.43, Figure 7 runs x 0-4 beside 0-0.2, Figure 8 y 0-25 beside 0-1.2, Figure 10 and Figure 11 differ on both axes - so every 'similar' or 'more obvious' claim in the prose is a claim about drawn shape, and the reader cannot check a magnitude without reading the ticks. Two families have no word in the vocabulary: the two eight-spoke radar pairs (Figure 4 and Figure 9) are filed as the nearest true description, and they are the paper's only charts that label every value and no ring, i.e. number tables wearing a chart costume. The only 3-D is sculptural - the framework pyramid of Figure 2 is drawn in isometric projection with visible side faces, and its three slabs assert an order (physiology at the base) that no weight in Table 1 supports, since the groups are never weighted between themselves. Legends are inside or above and always over the data. 

Tables. Three grids, all three measured, and only one of them a grid. Table 1 and Table 3 are the same drawing: three stacked vector blocks - Physiological need in three columns, Safety need in two, Society need in three - separated by heavy full-width rules, with thin rules under each header row, short vertical stubs between the columns of a block, no closed outer box, no shading, no unit in any header because the per-cent sign is welded into every cell. Both carry the SAME caption, 'The weights of indicators', and both are read as evidence for the same sentence, and the numbers differ everywhere: Import 10% folded into Production to make 74%, External intervention and Military deleted, Public order 21% to 11%, Terrorist attack 42% to 58%, Crimes 20% to 31%, Party 22% replaced by Subsidy 21%, Ethnic 18% gone, two factors that appear in no sentence of the body (Slums, Reservoir) printing in both. The prose says 'The weights are still similar to Table 1'. Table 1's twelve columns all sum to 100; Table 3's do not - Stability 101, Governance 99, Economics 111 - so the reallocation leaks eleven points. Table 2 is the only true grid and the only honestly quantitative exhibit: five columns, two header rows, country names merged over their condition columns, a double vertical rule between the two countries, three-heavy-rule booktabs, decimal-aligned to three places, and its summary row F is the one row the prose reads. No grid carries a unit in a header: the only unit anywhere in the paper is Figure 8's 'billion dollars', floated above a y axis where the title should be. 

Apparatus. Pagination is correct and clean - 'Page 2 of 21' on physical p4 and 'Page 21 of 21' on p28, so the folio runs one page behind the physical page throughout, and the contents page's numbers match the printed folio, not the physical page. A red Chinese resale banner prints across p4, p6, p8, p12, p14, p18, p23 and p25, twice directly over an exhibit (it cuts the upper frame of the flowchart on p4 and the top of Figure 10 on p23). The document-wide defect is the missing fi/ff/fl ligature: 'di erent', 'modi ed', 'Modi cation', 'signi cance', 'coe cient', 'e ciency' and 'in ation' are all printed with a gap where the ligature should be, in captions as well as prose, and one of the two weight tables spells its own column 'Sustainalibity'.
rules: A construction diagram heads the section that needs it and a result chart tails the section that produced it: the flowchart closes 1 Introduction, the framework pyramid opens 3.1, the impact taxonomy closes 3.2.1, and every exhibit after that is a computed quantity placed after the paragraph that reads it [place.section_kind].

Thirteen of the fourteen exhibits sit in five sections of two pages or fewer and the paper never places two unrelated exhibits on one page: the two on page 21 are read one after the other in the same subsection, and page 15 carries the table that the figure beside it plots [place.page_order].

Order runs figure, then caption, then prose: every one of the eleven figures prints its art ABOVE its caption and every one of the three tables prints the caption ABOVE its grid, without a single exception in 28 pages [caption.position].

The caption form is `Figure <n>: <noun phrase>` with a colon and no terminal verb - 'Figure 2: Framework of fragility model', 'Table 1: The weights of indicators' - and the tables use the same form, so caption style does not distinguish a grid from a chart [caption.numbering].

All fourteen captions are bare noun phrases of six to seventeen words, not one names a variable, a unit, a condition or a conclusion: the longest is seventeen words (the two radar and sensitivity panels) and the shortest is six ('Figure 1: Flowchart of our study'), so a reader who reads only captions learns the subject of every exhibit and the finding of none [caption.words].
Not one caption draws a conclusion and not one states a unit [caption.concludes].
No caption marks a variable as a variable [caption.variable_count].

Every caption is quoted from the text layer with its own damage intact - 'di erent', 'modi ed', '(a)Afghanistan' - because the ff and fi ligatures are missing throughout this document and a retyped caption would silently repair it [caption.verbatim].

Every caption is one sentence, and the panel key that should continue it rides a wrapped second line as a bare fragment - '(a) Afghanistan; (b) Egypt.' - so the key is printed twice, once clipped inside the artwork and once under it [caption.sentences].

Pointer style is `Figure <n> shows ...` for a result and `As shown in Figure <n>(a), ...` for a panel - three of the fourteen exhibits are introduced by the figure-n-shows form, seven by the as-shown-in form and four by a bare pointer with no connective at all, and the parenthetical form is used only for a re-reference [mention.lead_pattern].

Citation is dense and specific: every one of the eleven figures and all three tables is named by number at least once, and the two most-cited exhibits are the two that carry the argument - the framework pyramid with six pointers and the sensitivity pair with four [mention.count].

Two pointers run BACKWARD: Figure 7 is named on p19 and prints on p21, Figure 10 is named on p22 and prints on p23 - the paper places a figure where it finishes drawing it and reads it on the previous page [mention.lead_pages].

The reading sentence after a figure always starts from the pointer and states the one number the reader is meant to take away - '285% of Afghanistan GDP', 'when the fragility indicator is lower than 0.428' - never a description of the axes [mention.trail_sentence].

Every two-panel figure is ONE raster that holds both panels; panel letters are typeset inside that raster at the top-left of each panel, where the left one is clipped by the text margin on all seven of them [geometry.panel_count].

Panels never share a window: Figure 5 runs y 0.25-0.31 beside 0.36-0.43, Figure 7 x 0-4 beside 0-0.2, Figure 8 y 0-25 beside 0-1.2, Figure 10 y 0.22-0.38 beside 0.3-0.55 and Figure 11 both axes apart, and no caption ever says so, which makes every 'similar' claim in the prose a claim about shape only [geometry.shared_axes].Legends are inside the plot area when they exist, and they sit over the data: lower-left in Figure 5, upper-right in Figure 10, upper-left in Figure 11, mid-right in Figure 7, and only the radar pair of Figure 4 keys itself above the panels [geometry.legend].

No exhibit carries a colourbar and none carries a colour scale with a key: colour is keyed only by a legend inside or above the panels, never by a graded bar, so in Figure 4 and Figure 9 the near-white 'before' polygon is set so pale that it disappears against the page and no key can recover it [geometry.colorbar].The only 3-D in the paper is sculptural, not quantitative: the framework pyramid is drawn in isometric projection with visible side faces, and its three slabs encode an order the prose never states and the weights then contradict [geometry.three_d].

Radar charts are the paper's most-used chart outside the line plot and the closed family vocabulary has no word for them: two of the eleven figures are eight-spoke radar pairs, filed as the nearest true description [geometry.family].Where a chart cannot print a scale it prints the values: the two radars label every vertex (sixteen values per panel) and label no ring, so the labels are the only readable axis the figure has [geometry.data_labels].

Ticks are printed on six of the eleven figures, and the five that print none are the three drawings and the two radars - both of which label every value instead - so printed ticks is a reliable signal that an exhibit is a computation rather than a definition [geometry.printed_numbers].Panel arrangement is a single row of two in every composite figure, never a grid: the paper has no 2x2 and no three-panel layout anywhere in eleven figures [geometry.panel_layout].

A weight table in this paper is not a grid but a drawing: three stacked vector blocks with heavy full-width separators, thin rules under each header row, short vertical stubs between the columns of a block and no closed outer box, which is why the detector sees them while it misses every rule-only grid in the lane [table.rule_style].
Zero zebra shading in all three grids: where this document shades anything it shades a column title band, not alternate rows, so zebra is not a habit here [table.zebra].

Band titles are the only merged cells in the two weight tables - one cell spanning three, two and three columns - and Table 2 merges the country names across their condition columns and the label 'Indicators' down both header rows [table.merged_cells].

Only the one true data grid aligns decimals: Table 2's thirty-six three-decimal values sit on a decimal axis while both weight tables print '5.33%' beside '18%' with no alignment at all [table.decimal_aligned].

No grid prints a unit in its header and no grid prints one outside its frame: the weight tables put a per-cent sign inside every cell, and Figure 8 - the one exhibit with a unit at all - floats 'billion dollars' above its y axis where an axis title should be [table.units_in_header].
All three grids and the union of the weight-table fragments span the full text measure, and the two drawn ones slightly overrun it on both sides [table.width].
Header depth is two rows everywhere: a band or country row over a condition or column row, so a reader always needs the second header line to decode the first [table.header_rows].
No table continues across a page turn and no table repeats a header - the one long table, Table 1, fits on one page because it is a picture and cannot reflow [table.continued].
Every table prints portrait and full measure - there is no landscape page, no rotated grid and no transposed layout in the paper [table.orientation].
No grid uses a diagonal header stub, though both weight tables have exactly the two-way structure that would invite one [table.diagonal_header].

The two weight tables count sixteen printed rows each across them and the data grid counts eleven, so row count rises with the number of named factors rather than with the number of numbers [table.rows].

Numeric columns belong only to the data grid: the two weight tables carry zero numeric columns because every number is welded into a prose cell ('Price 26%, Import 10%'), which is why they cannot be sorted, compared or summed by a reader [table.numeric_cols].

Columns track the number of sub-factors per need group, not a house style: three columns in the physiological and society bands, two in the safety band, and the safety band drops from three to two between Table 1 and Table 3 without a word of explanation [table.cols].

Zones follow the prose, not a page grid: three exhibits sit at the top of a page, eight in the middle and three at the bottom, so a reader looking for a figure has to read the paragraph before it [place.page_zone].

No exhibit owns a page: the biggest is the union of Table 1's three blocks at 0.245 of the page and the largest single region is Figure 1 at 0.181, so every exhibit shares its page with prose [place.area_frac].
Every exhibit sits under a numbered heading and none is placed in an appendix or in the front matter [place.section_numbered].
Document order is page order is number order except for two backward pointers, so the sequence is broken by placement habit rather than by numbering errors [place.doc_order].

tables.note: Not a ruled grid: a drawing of a table, pasted in as three vector blocks - Physiological need (three columns), Safety need (two), Society need (three) - separated by heavy full-width rules and thin rules under each header row, with short vertical stubs between the columns inside a block and NO closed outer box, so the left and right edges are open and the block separators read as doubles where two blocks abut. Every band title spans its whole block (3, 2 and 3 columns), which is the only merged cell in the paper; there is no alternate-row shading, no diagonal and no unit in any header - the per-cent sign is printed inline in every cell, so a group weight (18%) and a sub-weight (64%) are typographically identical. Every column does sum to 100 - the eight superior weights divide 18/18/18 and 15/15 and 5.33 three times, and each inferior column closes on its parent - so the table is arithmetically sound and its twin on p24 is not. The paper reads it as evidence that 'physiology is the most important need' while the 18% band and the 5.33% band are simply group members with no between-group weight anywhere. The block is the largest exhibit in the paper once its three fragments are unioned (0.245 of the page) and it is one of the two grids the detector saw at all - precisely because it is a picture.

tables.note: The paper's one true grid and its one honestly quantitative table: five columns (Indicators | Afghanistan without / with climate change | Egypt without / with), nine row labels FD, WA, SH, SC, ST, EC, GN, DM and the summary F, two header rows with 'Indicators' spanning both and each country name spanning its two conditions, and a DOUBLE vertical rule between the Afghanistan and Egypt blocks. Three-heavy-rule booktabs with thin rules under each header row, open left and right edges, no shading, no diagonal, no unit anywhere - the values are unitless indices, which the caption does not say, so '0.271' has no stated scale. Decimals are aligned and that is the table's single typographic discipline. The summary row F is set off by a heavier rule above and it is the row the prose reads; the table also supplies the numbers Figure 4 then plots, so one page carries the measurement and the picture of the same measurement - the cleanest exhibit-to-evidence pairing in the paper.

tables.note: Table 1's twin, drawn by the same hand and pasted the same way: three open-sided vector blocks, band titles spanning their columns, percentages inline, no shading, no closed box, no unit in a header. What changed is the content, and the prose does not admit how much: the caption is IDENTICAL to Table 1's ('The weights of indicators') and the text says 'The weights are still similar to Table 1', yet every Safety number differs (External intervention 11% and Military 6% deleted, Public order 21% to 11%, Terrorist attack 42% to 58%, Crimes 20% to 31%, Refugee 29% to 25%, Violent con ict 62% to 48%, two new factors), the Safety block drops from three columns to two, Import 10% is folded into Production 64% to make 74%, Party 22% becomes Subsidy 21%, Ethnic 18% disappears, and two factors never mentioned in the body (Slums, Reservoir) print in both tables. The arithmetic is worse than Table 1's columns all summed to 100; this one's do not - Stability reaches 101, Governance 99 and Economics 111 - so the modification that the text describes as a deletion of factors is in fact a reallocation that leaks eleven points into the Economics column. Same caption, same drawing, different numbers, no reconciliation - a reader comparing the two tables has to do the subtraction themselves.
